On battery, Vivid Walls is deliberately conservative: it can pause automatically on battery power, pauses behind fullscreen apps, and idles when the desktop isn't visible. A wallpaper that moves with your music shouldn't cost you your afternoon charge.

Get started

Vivid Walls is live on the Mac App Store. $9.99, one-time, no subscription. The Windows Companion is free.

Download on the Mac App Store  See the transfer tutorial

## Frequently asked questions

Can a Mac wallpaper react to music? 

Not with anything built into macOS. Apple's dynamic and aerial wallpapers follow the clock, not your audio. Vivid Walls adds this: it runs Wallpaper Engine audio visualizer scenes natively on macOS, and they react in real time to whatever your Mac is playing, from any app. [...] The largest catalog of audio reactive wallpapers anywhere is the Wallpaper Engine Workshop on Steam, and that is countable rather than a figure of speech. The Workshop's own "audio responsive" filter returns 278,477 published items, close to one in ten of its 2,865,391 total, and 210,699 of those are scene-type wallpapers rather than video loops. All of it was built for a Windows-only app, since Wallpaper Engine is not available on Mac. Vivid Walls runs those same scene files natively on macOS, and the version 1.2 update adds the audio reactive behavior: play something in Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube, or a game, and the wallpaper reacts in real time. Treat those counts as the size of Wallpaper Engine's catalog rather than a promise about coverage: how much of a catalog that size renders [...] Does it work with Spotify and Apple Music? 

Yes. Audio reactive support shipped in the Vivid Walls 1.2 update, live now on the Mac App Store: it listens to the Mac's system audio output, so scenes react to Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube, games, or anything else making sound.

   Is the audio recorded or sent anywhere? 

No. The app reads the audio signal in the moment to compute levels and frequencies for the visualizer, and nothing is recorded, stored, or transmitted. Audio access uses the standard macOS permission prompt and can be revoked in System Settings at any time.
